question: Will any political party or coalition acquire a supermajority in the 2026 Hungarian parliamentary elections?
summary: Early-2026 polls are highly divergent with large undecided shares, which undermines confidence in a clear 2/3 outcome and justifies dialing down the ensemble.
Historical base-rate shows constitutional two-thirds majorities have occurred in only a subset of post-1990 elections, anchoring expectations downward from the 0.81 ensemble.
District-level dynamics and potential gerrymandering could tilt seat allocation in either direction, adding both upside and downside risk to the probability.
A 2/3 majority is possible but not strongly supported by current polling; the threshold requires substantial swings, making the final probability modest rather than high.

justification.critique_assessment: Objections are valid and reveal genuine blind spots (poll volatility, base-rate constraints, district effects) that collectively warrant tempering the ensemble; they do not imply an implausible scenario, but they reduce the likelihood of a 2/3 outcome.
justification.adjustment: Adjusted downward from the ensemble 0.81 to 0.60 to reflect the weight of divergent polls, undecided voters, and historical base-rate constraints; the adjustment respects the possibility of upside from opposition unity and district advantages but ultimately acknowledges substantial uncertainty.

forecasts.reference-class: Two-thirds majority (133+ seats) in the Hungarian National Assembly; historical base-rate since 1990 shows roughly 4 of the 9 post-1990 elections produced a constitutional two-thirds majority.

sources.claim: Financial Times reports opposition groups uniting behind the Tisza party and polling ahead of Fidesz, with indications of a possible 'Tisza supermajority' in some scenarios.
AP News notes the election date and reports polls showing Tisza leading vs Fidesz.
Euronews coverage describes split polls with Tisza leading in some surveys and mentions betting/prediction-market signals.
Hungary Today cites Real-PR seat projections via 21 Research Center suggesting Fidesz near a two-thirds share of seats.
Átlátszó discusses seat-based polling and potential dynamics (including district-level effects) that could influence whether a majority is reached.
Barclays notes forint could strengthen if the opposition wins, signaling market expectations of a possible government change.
DW reports the historical occurrence of Fidesz achieving a constitutional two-thirds majority (2010), illustrating the base-rate dynamics.
Wikipedia confirms Fidesz–KDNP won 263 of 386 seats in 2010, a two-thirds majority.
Wikipedia confirms Fidesz–KDNP secured a two-thirds majority in 2014.
Wikipedia confirms Fidesz won a two-thirds majority in 2018 (133 of 199 seats).
Wikipedia confirms Fidesz won a two-thirds majority in 2022 (135 of 199 seats).
AP News notes the 2024 European Parliament election context showing challenges to dominance, informing expectations for 2026 dynamics.
Britannica notes Fidesz has won two-thirds majorities in 2010, 2014, 2018, and 2022.
Euronews reports polls are divergent: some show Fidesz ahead, others show Tisza ahead; no clear consensus on who will reach a two-thirds majority.
Reuters reports that polls in early February 2026 show Tisza leading in some surveys and that the outcome remains uncertain with many voters undecided.
IDEA Intézet poll (Feb 6, 2026) shows TISZA at 48% and Fidesz at 38% (general population), not near the 2/3 threshold.
Publicus poll (Feb 15, 2026) shows TISZA at 48% and Fidesz at 39% among respondents, again far from a 2/3 share.
Republikon Intézet poll (Feb 12-17, 2026) shows TISZA leading with 47% vs Fidesz 39%.
IDEA Institute survey (early February 2026) finds Tisza leading (36% vs 28% for Fidesz) among all adults, with potential for a four-party parliament.
Polls show a split in leads across firms: some surveys put Tisza ahead, others show Fidesz ahead; multiple polls report varying margins and betting markets suggesting mixed expectations.
OSW reports Medián January polling indicating TISZA leads 51% to 39% among all voters (and other variants among decided voters), signaling no guaranteed path to a two-thirds majority.
Nézőpont poll (Nov 2025) cited by the China-CEE Institute shows Fidesz 47% vs Tisza 40% (with other polls showing narrower or reversed margins).
Financial Times reports opposition groups consolidating around Tisza ahead of the 2026 vote, with polls showing Tisza leading by varying margins depending on the survey.
